tasks.title: Audio: four-channel Synth
tasks.acceptance: dotnet build AnsiDemo.slnx -warnaserror && dotnet test AnsiDemo.slnx --no-build --filter "FullyQualifiedName~AnsiDemo.Tests.Audio.Synth"
tasks.prompt:
Implement `AnsiDemo.Audio.Synth` (spec reqs 6.1-6.5) in `src/AnsiDemo/Audio/Synth.cs`: `public sealed class Synth : ISynth` with a public parameterless constructor, on the merged contracts (`ISynth`, `Instrument`, `AudioFormat.SampleRate` = 44100, `AudioFormat.Channels` = 4). Another task writes the sinks in the same folder in parallel: you may only create files matching `src/AnsiDemo/Audio/Synth*.cs` and `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Audio/Synth*.cs` (a helper type goes in e.g. `SynthChannel.cs`; do not create a folder or namespace named `Synth`).

Behaviour:
- Channels 0 and 1 pulse, 2 triangle, 3 noise; each has value 0 until `NoteOn` and after `NoteOff`.
- `NoteOn(ch, f, instrument)`: phase = 0, envelope = 1, frequency f, keep the instrument's Duty, Volume, DecayPerSecond. Pulse: +1 while the phase fraction < Duty, else ΓêÆ1. Triangle: linear ΓêÆ1 ΓåÆ +1 over the first half period, +1 ΓåÆ ΓêÆ1 over the second. Noise: a 15-bit LFSR, reset to 1 on NoteOn, stepped 16┬╖f times per second (accumulate 16┬╖f/SampleRate per sample and step once per whole unit); a step is `bit = (lfsr ^ (lfsr >> 1)) & 1; lfsr = (lfsr >> 1) | (bit << 14)`; output +1 when bit 0 is set, else ΓêÆ1.
- `Render(Span<short> buffer)`: per sample write `(short)(Math.Clamp(0.25 * ╬ú value┬╖Volume┬╖envelope, -1, 1) * 32767)`, then advance every channel by one sample: phase += f/SampleRate (wrapped to 0..1), envelope = max(0, envelope ΓêÆ DecayPerSecond/SampleRate). So the first sample after NoteOn uses phase 0 and envelope 1.
- `SetFrequency` changes pitch only; `NoteOff` silences until the next NoteOn.
- `ArgumentException` when ch is outside 0..3, or f Γëñ 0 or f > SampleRate/2 (NoteOn and SetFrequency), or ch outside 0..3 in NoteOff.
- `double` math, no allocation in Render, no locking needed (the player calls it from one thread).

Tests in `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Audio/SynthTests.cs` (namespace `AnsiDemo.Tests.Audio`, `public class SynthTests`): silence before NoteOn; exact pulse samples for f = 441 Hz (period 100 samples) with duty 0.5 and 0.25 and the 0.25┬╖Volume scaling; triangle shape at quarter points; first noise samples against the LFSR computed in the test, and the 16┬╖f step rate; linear decay reaching and staying at 0; mixing of several channels and the clamp; SetFrequency keeps phase and envelope; NoteOff; restart on a second NoteOn; every ArgumentException case. Never edit `.csproj`/`.slnx`.

The Synth is written by another task in the same folder in parallel: you may only create files matching `src/AnsiDemo/Audio/*Sink*.cs`, `src/AnsiDemo/Audio/WaveOut*.cs` (e.g. `WaveOutNative.cs` for the P/Invoke) and `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Audio/*Sink*.cs`. Keep ΓëÑ 4 buffers of 2048 samples queued from a background feeder thread (IsBackground = true): fill each via `source.Render(Span<short>)` into a managed `short[]`, copy into unmanaged memory, `waveOutPrepareHeader` once, `waveOutWrite`, and refill a buffer when its WAVEHDR has WHDR_DONE (0x1) set (poll every few ms or use CALLBACK_EVENT). - `WavFileSink(string path, long totalSamples)`: `Start(source)` synchronously renders exactly `totalSamples` samples through `source.Render` (in chunks; the last chunk may be shorter) and writes a RIFF/WAVE file: canonical 44-byte header ("RIFF", 36 + dataBytes, "WAVE", "fmt ", 16, format 1, channels 1, 44100, 88200, block align 2, 16 bits, "data", dataBytes) then the samples little-endian; then returns. `Stop`/`Dispose` are no-ops; a second Start throws `InvalidOperationException`.

tasks.title: Tracker: Notes, SongParser, SongPlayer, RecordingSynth
tasks.acceptance: dotnet build AnsiDemo.slnx -warnaserror && dotnet test AnsiDemo.slnx --no-build --filter "FullyQualifiedName~AnsiDemo.Tests.Tracker"
tasks.prompt:
Implement the `tracker` module (spec reqs 8.1-8.6 and the 'Song format' of 4.3) in `src/AnsiDemo/Tracker/` (namespace `AnsiDemo.Tracker`, one type per file) on the merged contracts (`Song`, `Pattern`, `RowCell`, `Instrument`, `ISynth`, `ISampleSource`, `SongFormatException`, `AudioFormat`). Signatures are fixed in spec 4.3 'Module APIs'. The real Synth is not available to you; test against your own fake.

- `Notes.Frequency(midi)` = 440┬╖2^((midi ΓêÆ 69)/12). `Notes.Parse`: exactly 3 chars `[A-G](#|-)[0-8]`, midi = 12┬╖(octave + 1) + semitone (C-4 = 60, C#4 = 61, B-3 = 59, A-4 = 69); anything else throws `FormatException`.
- `SongParser.Parse(text)`: line-based; `;` starts a comment anywhere (`#` is a sharp, never a comment); blank lines ignored; accept both '\n' and '\r\n'; tokens separated by spaces; names match `[A-Za-z0-9_]+`; all numbers with `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture`. Directives: `bpm <int>` and `rows-per-beat <int>` (each once, positive, before the first pattern), `instrument <name> duty=<0.125|0.25|0.5> vol=<0..1> decay=<ΓëÑ0>` (before the first pattern), `pattern <name>` ΓÇª rows ΓÇª `end`, `order <name> ΓÇª` (after all patterns; several lines append). A row is split on `|` into exactly 4 trimmed cells; a cell is `---`, `off`, or `<note> <instrument> [v<0-9>] [a<X><Y>]` (optional parts in that order, X and Y hex digits) ΓåÆ `RowCell.Note(midi, instrumentIndex, volume, arpX, arpY)` (arp 0, 0 when absent). Result keeps instruments, patterns and order in file order; Order holds pattern indexes. Every violation listed in 8.2 (and a directive in the wrong place or repeated) throws `SongFormatException` with the 1-based line of the first problem; for things only known at the end (missing bpm, rows-per-beat or order, a pattern without `end`) use the last line number of the text.
- `SongPlayer(song, synth, loop)` (8.4-8.6): `Render(buffer)` walks the order list row by row. Row k of the whole song starts at sample `round(k ┬╖ SecondsPerRow ┬╖ 44100)` computed from the absolute row index (no drift). On a row's first sample, per channel 0..3: note cell ΓåÆ `synth.NoteOn(ch, Notes.Frequency(Midi), instrument)` where the instrument is `song.Instruments[i]`, or `with { Volume = Volume ┬╖ v / 9 }` when v is given; `off` ΓåÆ `NoteOff(ch)`; `---` ΓåÆ nothing. For a note with (ArpX, ArpY) Γëá (0, 0): `SetFrequency(ch, Frequency(Midi + ArpX))` at 1/3 of the row and `Frequency(Midi + ArpY)` at 2/3 (sample offsets rounded). Between events render through `synth.Render` on sub-spans of the buffer, so boundaries are sample-accurate for any buffer split. At the end of the order list: loop ΓåÆ start over at row 0 (position wraps to 0); otherwise NoteOff every channel once and write zeros. A song with 0 rows renders zeros. `PositionSeconds` = song samples played / 44100, `DurationSeconds` = `song.DurationSeconds`. `Paused` (volatile; set from another thread): Render writes zeros and does not advance. `Seek(t)` may be called from another thread: store it (Interlocked/lock) and apply at the start of the next Render: jump to the first row whose start time is ΓëÑ t (at or past the end behaves like the end of the order list) and call `NoteOff` on every channel. No allocation in Render in the steady state.
- `tests/AnsiDemo.Tests/Tracker/RecordingSynth.cs` (namespace `AnsiDemo.Tests.Tracker`) exactly as in spec 4.3 'Tracker test fake': `Calls` entries "On <ch> <hz:F2> <instrument name>", "Freq <ch> <hz:F2>", "Off <ch>" formatted with InvariantCulture; `Render` writes zeros and adds to `SamplesRendered`.

NoteOff on all channels). At bpm 125 and 4 rows per beat a row is exactly 5292 samples. Never edit `.csproj`/`.slnx`.
